Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

BrowseComp · filtered: The BrowseComp paper reports an initial 1,287-question set and removal of 21 questions with answer-format mismatches, ambiguous phrasing or incorrect answers, leaving 1,266 questions.

Permanent record ID: candidate.normal12.browsecomp.final-screening.v2

  • The paper says this review focused on the 118 questions where Deep Research had a zero pass rate; it was not an independent audit of every payload label.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

BrowseComp · has stage: The BrowseComp paper describes 1,266 human-written browsing questions designed to have stable short factual answers that are difficult to locate online; candidate questions were screened against models with and without browsing and against the first results pages from five Google searches.

Permanent record ID: candidate.normal12.browsecomp.human-construction.v2

  • This describes the original BrowseComp family, not the separate Mercor 130 subset or every browsing benchmark.
  • Difficulty screening is creator-reported and is not a performance ranking.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

BrowseComp · access terms: BrowseComp’s authors caution that its questions are not representative of typical user requests and ask that benchmark examples not be reproduced online to reduce contamination.

Permanent record ID: candidate.normal12.browsecomp.scope-and-contamination.v2

  • The paper’s public availability is not treated as a dataset-license clearance.
  • Long-form response quality, naturally ambiguous requests and all multimodal browsing tasks are outside the documented short-answer design.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

BrowseComp · evaluates: BrowseComp uses an AI grader to compare a submitted short answer with the reference answer for semantic equivalence; its appended grading instructions focus on answer matching rather than independently solving the question.

Permanent record ID: candidate.normal12.browsecomp.semantic-grading.v2

  • The grader prompt is a documented procedure, not an independently validated correctness oracle.
  • No benchmark question, answer or canary string is reproduced in this proposition.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

BrowseComp · human annotation: BrowseComp construction uses inverted question design from a chosen answer, reviews plausible answer uniqueness, and revises a question if another valid answer is found; second-trainer attempts were used for a portion of questions.

Permanent record ID: candidate.normal12.browsecomp.uniqueness-review.v2

  • The paper does not guarantee unique answers and does not establish a strict universal 10-minute second-review protocol for every question.
